title: A Phase 1 Study of JNJ-95804306 for Relapsed or Refractory Hematological Malignancies
official: A Phase 1, First-in-human, Dose Escalation Study of JNJ-95804306 for Relapsed or Refractory Hematological Malignancies
summary:
Main objective: Part 1 (Dose Escalation): To characterize the safety and tolerability of JNJ-
95804306 and identify putative RP2D regimen(s) in R/R AML/HR MDS and R/R CLL/SLL/NHL in monotherapy and in R/R AML/HR MDS and R/R CLL/SLL in combination therapy ; Part 2 (Dose Expansion): To further characterize the safety for JNJ-95804306 at the putative RP2D(s) in the expansion cohort(s)in R/R AML/HR MDS and R/R CLL/SLL/NHL monotherapy and in R/R AML/HR MDS and R/R CLL/SLL in combination therapy
conditions: Relapsed or Refractory higher-risk myelodysplastic syndromes
Relapsed or Refractory small lymphocytic lymphoma
Relapsed or Refractory chronic lymphocytic leukemia
Relapsed or Refractory acute myeloid leukemia
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. 1.At the time of informed consent, be ≥18 years of age or the legal age to provide informed consent in the jurisdiction in which the study is taking place.
2. 2. Diagnosis:  a.AML per ICC 2022 or MDS per WHO 2022 classified as moderate high, high, or very high-risk per the IPSS-M. If molecular results within the 12 months prior to informed consent are not available, participants must have IPSS-R >3.5, which corresponds with risk categories of intermediate, high-risk, or very high-risk MDS. (i) All participants must have relapsed or refractory disease and have exhausted or are ineligible for standard therapeutic options. Eligible participants will have a bone marrow blast burden ≥5%. Participants with newly transformed secondary AML may be enrolled at the investigator’s discretion, provided that no standard therapeutic options exist based on the treatment prior to transformation. b. CLL/SLL/NHL: All participants must have relapsed or refractory disease with no other approved therapies available that would be more appropriate in the investigator’s judgment.                                                                                                                    c. CLL/SLL meeting 2018 iwCLL NCI Working Group Guidelines that meet the following criteria: (i.) Participants must have received at least 2 prior lines of therapy.  (ii.) Have clinically measurable disease (lymphocytosis >5×10⁹/L and/or palpable and measurable nodes by physical exam and/or organomegaly assessed by physical exam) OR                                                                                                                    d. B-cell NHL as defined per the 2022 WHO classification: In addition, the following subtype-specific criteria outlined below must be met: (i.) If DLBCL: Previously treated with a minimum of 2 prior lines of systemic therapy, received, or not eligible for high-dose chemotherapy and autologous stem cell transplantation with curative intent. (ii.) If FL/MZL (except MALT) or WM: Previously treated with a minimum of 2 prior lines of systemic therapy, with at least one prior line containing an anti-CD20 antibody. Participants with transformed FL/MZL are eligible, with eligibility based on the transformed histology and its applicable treatment paradigm. (iii.) If MCL: Previously treated with at least 1 prior line of systemic therapy containing an anti-CD20 antibody.
3. 3. ECOG performance status score between 0 and 2
Exclusion criteria:
1. 1.Renal function: Have a CKD-EPIcr eGFR <60 mL/min computed with the 2021 CKD-EPI eGFRcr equation
2. 2.Hematology laboratory results: a.AML/MDS: leukocytes >25 × 109/L b.CLL: (i.) Hemoglobin: <8.0 g/dL, or use of transfusion or growth factors within 1 week; OR (ii.) Neutrophils: <1.0 × 103/µL (in case of documented bone marrow involvement of disease <0.75×103/µL), or use of transfusion or growth factors within 1 week; OR (iii.) Platelets: <25 × 103/µL, or use of transfusion or growth factors within 1 week or active mucosal bleeding or history of a spontaneous bleeding episode within three months of first dose of study treatment
3. 3.Chemistry laboratory results  a. AST and ALT: >3 × ULN, unless there is documented liver involvement by disease with the exclusion threshold at >4 × ULN, OR b. Total bilirubin:  >1.5 × ULN, OR bilirubin in case of known congenital nonhemolytic indirect hyperbilirubinemias such as Gilbert’s Syndrome may demonstrate isolated total bilirubin ≥1.5 × ULN with conjugated [direct] bilirubin >1.5 × ULN. Note: Gilbert’s syndrome is suggested by direct bilirubin <30% (Palmer 2020), OR c. AML participants receiving combination treatment: albumin <3.0 mg/dL
4. 4. Have evidence of uncontrolled systemic viral, bacterial, or fungal infection. Antimicrobial prophylaxis is permitted
5. 5. Had major surgery (eg, requiring general anesthesia) or had significant traumatic injury within 2 weeks before screening, or will not have fully recovered from surgery, or has surgery planned during the time the participant is expected to participate in the study
6. 6. Had any of the following within 6 months prior to start of study treatment: severe or unstable angina, myocardial infarction, major thromboembolic events (eg, pulmonary embolism, cerebrovascular accident), clinically significant ventricular arrhythmias or heart failure NYHA functional classification Class III – IV
7. 7. Has known active CNS involvement
8. 8. Any of the following prior therapies: a. AML/MDS:  (i.) Chemotherapy (with the exception of hydroxyurea and/or a single dose of cytarabine up to 1 g/m2 as noted above) within 2 weeks of first dose of study drug. (ii.) Local radiation within 7 days of first dose of study drug. Note: must have at least 1 measurable lesion beyond what is irradiated. (iii.) Antibody use within 2 weeks of first dose of study drug. (iv.) Targeted therapy (with the exception of a BCL2 targeting agent) or investigational agents within 2 weeks or 5 half-lives, whichever is shorter, of first dose of study drug. (v.) A BCL2 targeting agent within 2 weeks of first dose of study drug.                                     (vi) Other targeted therapy (with the exception of a BCL2 targeting agent) or investigational agents within 2 weeks or 5 half-lives, whichever is shorter, of first dose of study drug. b. CLL:  (i.)  Chemotherapy or immunotherapy within 2 weeks before the first administration of study drug.  (ii.) Local radiation within 7 days of first dose of study drug.  (iii.) Monoclonal antibody (single target) use within 4 weeks of first dose of study drug.                                          (iv.) A BCL2-targeting agent within 2 weeks of first dose of study drug.                           (v.)For  other targeted therapies, inclusive of T-cell engagers, and investigational agents where the half-life is known, there should be a treatment-free window of at least 2 weeks or 5 half-lives, whichever is shorter.
